text: The team filter is an optional additive query parameter on GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases, combined with the other filters by AND inside the caller's scope, and it is published in the baseline as an addition to the request list of API-P3-001; the export operation keeps the team parameter it already lists in API-P3-017.
why: The legacy flow, scenario AC1 and FSD A2.19 filter by queue, team and status, the legacy section 12 adds the team parameter, and the technical specification lists it for the export only, so the list operation needs one stated answer; and it stays optional so no existing consumer breaks.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-031 sections 4 and 12; TSD P3 v3 T-A.2 API-P3-001 and API-P3-017; FSD P3 v4 A2.19; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-11
confirm: Solution architect with the gateway-bff owner in the baseline review of RWB-P3-E1031-CON.
impact: If the team parameter is refused on the list, one query parameter, one filter control and AC1 of the flow change; no schema, event or workflow change.

text: rwb-case returns ownerUserId on every case row and never a display name; the display name is resolved at the edge by gateway-bff against the ACE Common user directory, and a case with no owner returns the field absent so the screen shows a blank owner cell.
why: The legacy story takes owner display names from the ACE user directory in the common module, no target source says which service resolves a staff name, and Architecture v5 slide 10 puts the merge of case and source-data answers in gateway-bff, so the answer must be stated once and held by one owner.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-031 sections 3, 5 (X5) and 11; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 10; TSD P3 v3 T3.1 (owner_user_id); Template and Rules R5.5 DP-19
confirm: Solution architect with the gateway-bff owner and the ACE Common owner before the story's Done.
impact: If rwb-case must return a name, one field and one user-directory read are added to the row and to the fake; no schema or event change, and no name is ever stored.

text: The access-log entry is written through the rwb-access access-log operation of RWB-P4-E1039-CON at POST /api/recovery/access/v1/access-events, one hop with a 2 s timeout and no retry on the export path, carrying eventCode AC-EXPT with the actor user reference, the time, the area Case record, the right R, the filter set and the row count; a failure answers 503 with MSG-P7-003 and no file is made, and the 401 and 403 texts are the rwb-access ones.
why: The legacy story names the Java interface AccessEventPublisher and its fields but no operation, and the split moves the access log to rwb-access, so the consumed row, its fake and the refusal of AC5 need one stated surface.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-031 sections 4 step 7, 5 (X3), 12 and 14; Architecture v5 slide 8 (access and PII logging in ACE Common, access service P4); Template and Rules R5.5 DP-11
confirm: P4 owner of rwb-access in the baseline review of RWB-P4-E1039-CON, with the rwb-case service owner.
impact: If the operation path or the field set differs, one consumed row, the AccessEventClient adapter, one fake and the AC2 assertion change; no case data and no event topic change.

text: The masking rules of the caller's role travel in the rwb-access authorise answer and are applied by rwb-case when it builds the workbook; rwb-case holds no copy of a masking row and calls no separate masking service.
why: Legacy BR4 applies the masking rules inside the module while the target policy belongs to rwb-access, and no source says whether the policy is applied by the case service or by a service of its own, so the export needs one stated owner of the act and one of the rule.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-031 section 8 BR4, section 13 (FieldMasker, RWB-E1-037); Technical Specifications by Module v5 TSD P3 v3 T6; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-08
confirm: rwb-access owner and the data steward at the baseline review of RWB-P4-E1037-CON.
impact: If masking moves to a separate answer, one cached client call and its fake are added and the workbook writer is unchanged; no column is added or removed.

text: caselist.export.maxrows stays 10,000 as a parameter row with the version in force, the page-size default 50 and maximum 200 stay the parameter rows of RWB-P3-E2011-APP, and the rwb-case login name is taken from the platform naming rule at deployment rather than fixed in this story.
why: The legacy story assumes 10,000 under DL11 and gives no page bounds, the queue-view story publishes the bounds, and the per-service login has no name in any source, so each value needs one stated home.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-031 sections 3, 8 BR5 and 13; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-02, DP-06; context pack P3 (schema rwb_case, one login per service)
confirm: Business owner for the row limit at UAT, and the platform DB owner for the login name.
impact: A limit or page-bound change is a parameter row change; a login change is a deployment value; no code, contract or schema change.

text: The feature switch keeps the legacy name rwb.p3.caselistqueue and is carried as a platform feature flag: off, the list hides the queue and owner columns and the export, and the parameters and lists are still read.
why: The legacy story names the flag and its off behaviour, and the platform flag library replaces the local property without a source giving a new name, so the legacy name is kept rather than invented.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-031 section 13 (feature flag); context pack P3 naming rules; Template and Rules R5.5 (no DP row for flags)
confirm: Platform library owner at the baseline review.
impact: A rename is one flag key and one values-file line; no code path and no contract change.

text: The baseline publishes the row schema as CaseListRow with the legacy field names caseNo, productGroup, status, stageCode, queueId, queueCode, queueName, ownerUserId (optional), teamCode, regionCode and entryDate, the page as CaseListPage with items, page, size and total, no cursor token, a default page size and a maximum read as parameter rows, and the 401 text from the rwb-access contract.
why: The legacy story fixes the fields and the page members but not the schema or envelope names, the sort token or the 401 text, and the technical specification gives only CasePage and Case, so the baseline cannot be frozen without one stated naming default.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-031 sections 11, 12 and 14; TSD P3 v3 T-A.2 API-P3-001; FSD P3 v4 A2.19.3.2; Template and Rules R7.2 s12
confirm: Service owner of rwb-case at the version freeze, with the gateway-bff owner.
impact: A rename is one schema change inside major version 1 and one regenerated type set on the consumer side; no table, event or workflow change.

text: The export answers 200 with the spreadsheet content type of the legacy story synchronously and stores no file of its own, and the index ix_case_team_status on recovery_case (team_code, status) that the legacy migration asked for is published in the baseline and landed on the rwb-case Flyway sequence by this legacy key, unless the case-list story already lands the same two columns.
why: The legacy story gives the export as a response of the same request and asks for one index, and no source says which story lands it after the split, so the contract and the sequence need one stated home.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-031 sections 12 and 13 (V031_1__case_team_index.sql); TSD P3 v3 T-A.2 API-P3-017; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-15
confirm: rwb-case service owner and the ACE DB team at the baseline review.
impact: A duplicate index is dropped before the migration is released; a change of response shape would need an asynchronous export, which no source asks for.
